title: Cardiac Priorities: Chest Pain, Heart Failure, Digoxin

questions.stem: A client reports chest pain. The oxygen saturation is 96%. Which action is correct?

options.text: Start oxygen right away for all chest pain
Oxygen is not needed unless saturation is below 90%
Start oxygen at the highest flow

questions.explanation: B is correct: oxygen is given if the saturation is below 90%, and 96% is above that. A and D give oxygen routinely, which doesn't help when saturation is normal. C is wrong because oxygen depends on the saturation, not on nitroglycerin.

questions.stem: How soon should a 12-lead electrocardiogram be obtained for a client with chest pain?
questions.explanation: A is correct: get a 12-lead electrocardiogram within 10 minutes. B, C, and D delay it.

questions.stem: A client with chest pain took sildenafil this morning. Nitroglycerin is ordered. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Hold the nitroglycerin and notify the provider

questions.explanation: B is correct: nitroglycerin is never given with erectile dysfunction drugs like sildenafil because the blood pressure can crash, so the nurse holds it and notifies the provider. A, C, and D still give it.

questions.stem: Which findings point to left-sided heart failure? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: A, B, and C are correct: left equals lungs, so fluid backs into the lungs. D and E are right-sided failure, where fluid backs into the body.

questions.stem: Which finding is most consistent with right-sided heart failure?

options.text: Swollen neck veins and ankle edema

questions.explanation: C is correct: right-sided failure backs fluid into the body, causing swollen neck veins and swollen ankles. A, B, and D are lung findings of left-sided failure.

questions.stem: A client with heart failure weighed 180 lb yesterday and 183 lb today. What should the nurse do?
questions.explanation: B is correct: a gain of 3 lb in a day meets the rule to report 2 to 3 lb in a day; that's fluid, not fat. A delays. C adds fluid. D is wrong because the gain is not normal.

questions.stem: How should a client with heart failure weigh themselves at home?

options.text: Same time, same scale, same clothes, every morning
Once a week in the evening

questions.explanation: B is correct: same time, same scale, same clothes, every morning. A, C, and D make the weights inconsistent or too infrequent.

questions.stem: Digoxin is due. The apical pulse is 54. What is the first action?

options.text: Hold it and notify the provider per parameters
Recheck in 4 hours, then give it

questions.explanation: B is correct: an adult apical pulse under 60 means hold digoxin and notify the provider per parameters. A and D give a dose to a client with a pulse under 60. C changes the dose without the provider.

questions.stem: A client takes digoxin. Which findings suggest toxicity? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: A, B, C, and D are correct: these are the signs of digoxin toxicity taught. E is a heart failure finding, not a toxicity sign.

questions.stem: A client on digoxin has a low potassium level. Why is this a concern?

options.text: It makes digoxin toxicity more likely
It has no effect on digoxin

questions.explanation: B is correct: low potassium makes digoxin toxicity more likely. A and D understate the risk: low potassium increases digoxin's effect on the heart. C is wrong because low potassium doesn't cause high blood pressure.
